title: Communicative Functions V1.0
description: What the A-User means to do with its body while it utters the Text of a Final Response: for each function, towards whom or what, with which words, how markedly and, at Level 2, with which behaviour. Basic Knowledge gives the functions in the Final Response (Level 1 or 2); Final Response Demultiplexing gives them to Behaviour Planning, which gives them to Animation Object Generation with a behaviour and its times for every function. The Function and the Behaviour are taken from closed lists, and a Behaviour shall be one of those allowed for its Function.

FinalResponseID.description: Identifier of the Final Response whose Text the functions go with.

Level.description: 0: no functions. 1: functions without behaviour. 2: functions, each of which may carry the behaviour that realises it.

FunctionName.description: Gaze: looks at the Target. Deictic: indicates the Target. Greeting: greets or takes leave of the Target. Affirmation: says yes or agrees. Negation: says no or disagrees. Beat: marks the words of the Anchor as important. Iconic: depicts the shape, size or movement of what the Anchor names. Metaphoric: gives a concrete form to an abstract idea. Uncertainty: shows doubt. Attention: shows that it listens to or attends to the Target. Invitation: invites the Target to act or to speak. Stop: asks the Target to stop or to wait.

BehaviourName.description: LookAt: eyes, and head if needed, towards the Target. TurnTowards: head, torso or whole body towards the Target. Point: index finger towards the Target. HeadPoint: a short head movement towards the Target. Nod: head down and up. HeadShake: head left and right. HeadTilt: head tilted to one side. Wave: open hand moved side to side. Bow: torso bent forward and back. Smile: a social smile. RaiseEyebrows: both eyebrows raised. Frown: brows drawn together. Shrug: shoulders raised and dropped. PalmUp: open hand, palm up. HoldOut: hand held out towards the Target, as when offering. StopPalm: hand raised, palm towards the Target. Stroke: a short downward hand movement on the peak word. Trace: the hand draws a shape or a path. Frame: two hands show a size or a boundary. LeanForward: torso leaning towards the Target.

FunctionID.description: Identifier of the function, unique in the Final Response; A-User Formation reports on it.

Target.description: Towards whom or what. Absent when the Function has no target.

ID.description: Identifier of the Item or of the M-Location, as the PC Prompt gives it.

Anchor.description: Where in the utterance the function goes. Words are the words of the Text, separated by white space, counted from 0.

Intensity.description: How marked the function is, from 0 to 1.

Requirement.description: Required: A-User Formation realises it or says why not. Optional: A-User Formation may leave it out.

Behaviour.description: Level 2 only. The behaviour that realises the function.

TowardsTarget.description: Whether the behaviour is directed towards the Target.

PeakWord.description: The word of the Anchor on which the peak of the behaviour falls.

Times.description: Given by Behaviour Planning only: start, peak and end of the behaviour, in seconds from the start of the Machine Speech.
